Colour temperature which has a fundamental influence on modern society. In this study, we analyse the psychological responses of
143 students in a memory task in a virtual classroom using three illuminance levels (100 lx, 300 lx and 500 lx)
and four colour temperatures (3000 K, 4000 K, 6500 K and 10500 K). The results showed that lighting conditions

and, in turn, provide better cognitive outcomes for students.

The perspective of a student sitting in the centre of the second row of
tables was taken as the viewpoint. The renders (one for each ALP) were
saved as cubic panoramas with a resolution of 2000 ×2000 pixels per
side. Fig. 4 shows the IVE replica of the educational environment.
The IVE experience was created through a head-mounted display
(HMD), in this case, the HTC Vive device. All the 360◦panoramas were
implemented in Unity3D (v5.6). The HTC Vive device offers a resolution
of 1080 ×1200 pixels per eye (2160x1200 in total), a field of view of
110◦ and a refresh rate of 90 Hz. The HMD was connected to a high-
performance computer (i9-10900 K CPU, 64 GB RAM, and an
RTX3080 GPU) to ensure a smooth experience.
Before starting the generation of the different ALPs, two actions were
carried out to ensure the accurately of the virtual replicate. First, the
HMD was calibrated to ensure the consistency of the colours reproduced,
by conducting visual comparisons with a calibrated screen by the
research team. Then, with the HMD calibrated, an environmental
simulation test was run: five participants in the educational environ-
ment judged the comparability of the IVE, first at the general level in an
open way and then at the level of illumination with the help of a series of
concepts (pleasantness, overall brightness, overall diffuseness, contrast,
uniformity, shadow visibility, coziness, liveliness, tenseness, and
detachment) identified by Murdoch et al. [129]. According to this test,
slight modifications were made to the textures of the materials. With this
procedure, the IVE could be used effectively for the purposes of this
study.
